name: Fertility Tracker API
description: Fertility, births, deaths, net migration, migrant stocks, UN projections to 2100 (medium and constant-fertility scenarios) and a population-decline risk score for every country. Static files, no key, CORS open, refreshed weekly.

endpoints.description: Summary for every country + WLD (sorted by iso3).
Full record for one country: series 1950-2100, demographic balance, migrant stocks and corridors, risk detail.
Countries ranked by population-decline risk + methodology.
Population of every country + WLD each year: UN estimates 1950-2023, then 2024-2100 under two UN WPP 2024 scenarios: medium ("UN forecast") and constant fertility ("If birth rates stay the same").
One row per country; nested fields flattened with underscores (components_births, projection_change2100Pct, ...).

Long format iso3,year,variant,metric,value. Metrics: population, births, deaths, naturalChange, netMigration, populationChange, tfr, medianAge, share65, immigrants, immigrantsPct, emigrants, emigrantsPct, livingAbroadPct. Rows with no data are omitted.
When the weekly refresh last ran and whether it succeeded (written at deploy time; generatedAt elsewhere only moves when numbers change).

dataGaps: Gross annual migration flows (how many people arrive and how many leave each year) are not published for all countries by any global source. We publish annual net migration (UN WPP: immigrants minus emigrants) plus migrant stocks from UN DESA as inflow/outflow proxies: immigrants = people living in a country who were born elsewhere; emigrants = people born in a country who now live abroad.

UN WPP 2024 estimates end in 2023; later years are the UN medium-variant projection (variant = "projection"). The demographic balance (components) and projection baselines use the latest estimate year. The next WPP revision is due 11 July 2027.

Togo follows the UN's interim update of 19 January 2026 (revised population and vital events, estimates and medium projection). The UN did not revise Togo's other scenarios or the world and regional aggregates; scenarios.json rescales Togo's constant-fertility path to the revised level (see its adjustments).

Headline fields (population, tfr, birthRate, deathRate, netMigration, populationGrowthPct, share65) take the newest year across World Bank and UN; each carries its own year and source. World Bank's latest net migration (and, for many countries, population) are themselves UN WPP estimates or projections.
populationChange = births - deaths + netMigration for the calendar year (UN WPP). It can differ slightly from the difference between successive 1 July population figures.

Migrant stocks are available for 1990-2020 every 5 years plus 2024; there is no annual series. migrantStock.emigrantsPct follows UN DESA / OWID: emigrants as % of the country's CURRENT RESIDENT population. livingAbroadPct is the share of everyone born in the country who lives abroad: emigrants / (residents - immigrants + emigrants).

projection.change2050Pct / change2100Pct are relative to projection.basePopulation in projection.baseYear (UN WPP, latest estimate year), not to the headline population (often a newer World Bank figure).
Taiwan and 20 small territories are not in the World Bank database: their figures come from UN sources only, their region is borrowed from a neighbour, and incomeGroup is null.
Places with fewer than 100,000 people are scored where possible but not ranked: small numbers make rates noisy.
